name: tts
description: Convert text to speech and save as an audio file. Uses pyttsx3 (offline) or an API.

manual.overview: Use when you need to convert text to spoken audio—accessibility, voiceovers, or audio versions of content. Uses pyttsx3 offline by default.

input.text: Welcome to our application. Log in to continue.

examples.description: Generate a welcome message for an app

input.text: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

tips: Keep chunks under ~500 chars for stable output; split long text into segments
Adjust rate (default 150) lower for clarity, higher for brisk narration
Output format depends on backend; pyttsx3 may produce WAV instead of MP3
edge_cases: Special characters or emoji in text can cause synthesis errors or be skipped
pyttsx3 quality varies by OS; Windows often sounds better than Linux

executor.command: python -c "import pyttsx3; e=pyttsx3.init(); e.setProperty('rate',{{args.rate}}); e.save_to_file('{{args.text}}','{{args.output_path}}'); e.runAndWait(); print('Saved to {{args.output_path}}')"
